links.why: cl0 is the first clause of the verse; there is no earlier clause within the verse for a then-link to come from, and this one runs backward
two commands joined by waw, one imperative group
a weqatal continues whatever it follows; the when-clause is the nearest clause before it, though it is a setting and not the main line
a command then waw and a yiqtol in a different person gives a purpose, not a plain and
let my people go, so that they may serve me: the yiqtol in the third person after a second-person command
he said to Moses introduces a collection of commands (rise early, present yourself); the speech that follows is the commanded turn
you will say to him introduces the message thus says the LORD
thus says the LORD introduces a command with its purpose, the imperative group

groups.why: the outer turn is the LORD speaking to Moses; the commanded turn to Pharaoh is nested as a part, so the cl5 clause moves into it
Moses is commanded to say the message to Pharaoh; the message quoting the LORD is its innermost part, so Moses is the sender of this turn
the innermost turn is the message thus says the LORD, so its sender is the LORD and it is addressed to Pharaoh; it is now a part of the commanded turn
rise early and present yourself are commands joined by waw at one level, so both are command members
let my people go is the command; so that they may serve me is its aim
